dependencies.rationale: The leanest possible graph: exactly the starter toolchain at current versions, no CSS/UI library (spec forbids), nothing the platform or framework already covers.

evidence: app/src/lib/server-api.ts:1-171 — all API access behind one module with an in-memory promise cache
app/src/lib/types.ts:1-47 — typed view models at the loader→component boundary
app/src/routes/moves/[name]/index.tsx:19-44 — loader maps raw API data to the typed view model, components never touch wire shapes
app/src/lib/server-api.ts:21 — api<T = any> defaults to any; app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:97 casts varieties with (v: any); server-api.ts:78,94 return Promise<any[]>
app/vite.config.ts:1-22 with app/adapters/node-server/vite.config.ts:1-19 — configuration centralized and derived via extendConfig, matching generator output
app/src/root.tsx:4, app/src/entry.node-server.tsx:17 — QwikCityProvider/createQwikCity are the only v2-renamed surfaces (QwikRouterProvider/createQwikRouter per next.qwik.dev/docs/upgrade)
churn_resistance.rationale: Data access, view models and configuration are each behind one well-defined module, and the boilerplate matches what the current generator emits, so a framework upgrade touches a handful of starter-owned files and no business logic. The weak spot is `any` at the API boundary: types.ts protects components but not the wire format, so PokeAPI shape changes would surface as runtime bugs rather than type errors.

findings.issue: The API boundary is effectively untyped: api<T = any> defaults to any, allTypes()/allGenerations() return Promise<any[]>, and loaders cast inline (e.g. (v: any) in app/src/routes/pokemon/[name]/index.tsx:97), so the typed view models in src/lib/types.ts guard only one side of the boundary.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI resources (Species, Pokemon, Type, Move, Ability, Generation) in src/lib/types.ts and type api<Resource>() at each call site so API shape changes fail the build instead of surfacing at runtime.

findings.issue: Server-side fetches have no timeout or AbortSignal; a slow or hung API request will hold the SSR render open indefinitely.
findings.suggestion: Pass { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(10_000) } to fetch and map aborts to a friendly error.

findings.issue: Qwik packages live only in devDependencies — correct for the v1 starter convention, but Qwik v2 requires @qwik.dev/core in dependencies when a production server loads Qwik libraries from node_modules (next.qwik.dev/docs/upgrade, 'Move qwik packages [...] to devDependencies').
findings.suggestion: Nothing to change on v1; note it for the v2 migration so `npm install --omit=dev` deploys don't break the server.

findings.issue: The debounce handler re-parses window.location.href to read the current query instead of the router's own location state, duplicating a source of truth the framework already exposes.
findings.suggestion: Track useLocation().url's q parameter (or keep the last-submitted value in a signal) instead of reading window.location directly.

findings.issue: The app ships no tests of its own (0 test files); correctness rests entirely on the external acceptance suite.
findings.suggestion: Add a few Vitest/Playwright cases for the pure logic most likely to regress (humanize, latestFlavorText, sortRows, moveTables) so refactors — including the eventual v2 migration — are guarded.

summary: This is a current-generation Qwik City app: pinned to the newest stable 1.20.3 (released days before today), using routeLoader$/useTask$/resolveValue throughout, no deprecated v1 APIs, and handler signatures that are already v2-compatible. Dependencies are minimal and modern, all data access sits behind one typed-view-model module, and the boilerplate matches what the current generator emits. The only real forward-looking gaps are an untyped `any` API boundary beneath the otherwise-clean view models and the absence of fetch timeouts on the server.
